case_name: Jafar Imam Naqvi v Election Commission of India
respondent:
Election Commission of India
Supreme Court of India

15  May  2014
W.P. (C) No. 429 of 2014
The Judgment was delivered by : Dipak Misra, J.
1. The petitioner, a practising advocate of this Court, as pro bone publico has preferred this writ petition with Art. 32 of the Constitution with the following prayers:
"(a) Issue a writ of mandamus in public interest or any other appropriate writ, order, direction, commanding respondent to take stern action against everyone and anyone found guilty as per law in view of the ongoing activities of the accused politicians and political parties and to ensure protection of the security of Election Staff posted at Varanasi and of public at large of the entire country;
(b) Issue a writ of mandamus in public interest or any other appropriate writ, order, direction commanding Respondent to withdraw the recognition given to such political parties resorting to illegal activities and to cancel the candidature of politicians found guilty bef
facts: The petitioner, a practising advocate of this Court, as pro bone publico has preferred this writ petition with Art.

The basic assertions in the petition relate to speeches which have been delivered during the recently finished election campaign by various leaders of certain political parties and how they have the effect potentiality to affect the social harmony.
Various examples have been given and certain newspaper clippings have been annexed.
issues: Whether the Court in exercise of power under Art. 32 of the Constitution should enter into the arena of effect and impact of election speeches rendered during the election campaign in a public interest litigation.
Whether the principle stated in Vishaka's case 1997 Indlaw SC 2304 and the principles laid down in other decisions are really not attracted to the present case.
petitioner_arguments: Since the infancy of the Constitution, this Court has not declined to declare a law wherever it has found that it is unConstitutional.
The Court expanded the concept of public remedy where there had been violation of fundamental rights and further opined that the concept of sovereign immunity would be not applicable.
The Court as a wing of the State is by itself a source of law.
court_reasoning: We find that the issue decided therein has nothing to do with the case of the present nature.
Thus, the said decision has no applicability to the case in hand.

The Court has consistently clarified that the directions have been issued by the Court only when there has been a total vacuum in law, i.e. complete absence of active law to provide for the effective enforcement of a basic human right.
holding: We request the Law Commission to also examine the issues raised herein thoroughly and also to consider, if it deems proper, defining the expression 'hate speech' and make recommendations to the Parliament to strengthen the Election Commission to curb the menace of 'hate speeches' irrespective of whenever made.
